item.title: Show HN: Is Hormuz open yet?
Show HN: Tired of logic in useEffect, I built a class-based React state manager
item.description:
📝 TL;DR: I built Snapstate to move business logic out of React components and into plain TypeScript classes. The trouble starts when application logic moves into that same layer. I wanted a place where that logic could exist without carrying React around with it.
🔗 Read more: https://thales.me/posts/why-i-built-snapstate/

item.title: Newly created Polymarket accounts win big on well-timed Iran ceasefire bets
